title: Smt results row
description: One line of the results of SmtRun (the blob Smt.CollectResults hands out): a row of the problem set, in the set's order, refused rows included. A row says how its problem was settled and what the answer is; it names no machine: how many copies answered and whether they agreed, never which. Models and values are the solver's own text, cut for what a lab sees at 65,536 bytes of UTF-8 a row (whole texts only, in the order the session gave them; model_truncated says so, and the full models stay in the run's ledger).

index.description: The row's place in the set, from 0: taken and refused rows are counted, blank lines are not.

id.description: The row's id; empty for a refused row whose id could not be read.

query.description: What was asked of the problem. Absent for a row the set refused.

logic.description: The logic the problem's set-logic names, as the host read it; empty for none. Absent for a row the set refused.

status.description: ok: the query was answered (an unknown included). refused: the set or the sanitizer refused the row, or a node refused the problem; no solver ran. input_error: the solver reported an error in what it was given. output_exceeded: the session wrote more than its output cap; the verdict the solver had given by then stands, its model is not there. engine_crash: the solver trapped, ended with a status that is no answer, or answered something unreadable. no_result: no node answered the problem, after the repair round either; code says what the nodes said last. disputed: the copies disagreed and three more did not settle it; code is the dispute's outcome. A no_result or a disputed row is no answer and is left out of the verdict counts.

code.description: The fixed word of the status: the refusal's code, the kind of a crash, the reason of a no_result (a node's fault code, a reason a result was refused, no_answer), the outcome of a standing dispute; empty where the status says it all.

message.description: The sentence that goes with the code: a refusal's reason (never the problem's text), the solver's message of an input error; empty for an answered query.

line.description: For a row the set refused: the line inside the problem's text the sanitizer refused, 0 for a refusal of the row itself.

reason.description: Why a check has no verdict or an enumeration is not complete: the resource limit of a check, the fuel of the hard cap, the memory, the solver's own word; none otherwise. other also for an enumeration that ended with the models it had found because the solver did not take a found model's values back.

expected.description: The verdict the row or the problem's :status expects; none for a proof.

expected_agreement.description: agree or disagree when a verdict sat or unsat meets an expected one; n/a otherwise.

complete.description: enumerate: the last check said unsat, so count is exact.

limit_reached.description: enumerate: as many models were found as were asked for.

proof.description: prove: unsat of the problem with the negated goal is proved; sat is a counterexample, with its model.

model.description: check and prove: the answer of (get-model) as the solver printed it; null without one or when it did not fit the row.

values.description: check: the answer of (get-value ...) for the terms the row asked for; null without them or when it did not fit. The host's evaluator holds it to those terms and to the model (validation).

models.description: enumerate: each model found, with the values of the projected constants that tell it apart.

model_truncated.description: Whether a model or a value of the row was left out (null above) because the row's texts passed 65,536 bytes.

validation.description: What the host's model evaluator said of every model of a sat answer and of the values that came with it, checked against the problem as the host sanitized it (the counterexample of a proof against the problem and the negated goal): validated, every assertion true and every value the row reports the value its term has under the model; failed, an assertion false or a reported value another than its term's, with nothing guessed; partial, neither (the reason says why: also values that are not those of the terms the row asked for). The worst of an enumeration's models. none: no model to check.

validation_reason.description: The evaluator's reason code of a partial or failed class (assertion_false or value_mismatch for failed; output_exceeded for a model that did not come whole); empty otherwise.

validation_detail.description: For a failed class: which assertion, or for value_mismatch which of the values asked, by its place from 1 (and which model of an enumeration).

copies.description: How many answers the problem was ruled on: the first fan-out's, the repair round's for a problem it sent out again, and the dispute round's. Answers of different fan-outs may be one machine's; settled_by says what the answer rests on. Never which machines.

agreed.description: Whether all of them gave one digest.

settled_by.description: one_copy: one machine's answer, nothing against it: one answer, or a lone answer of the first fan-out and a lone answer of the repair round with the same digest (two fan-outs may place them on one machine). copies: two or more with one digest, two of them of one fan-out (the first, or the repair round), whose copies are on different machines. dispute: the majority of three more machines after the first copies disagreed or the evaluator called the model failed. agreement: the machines agree and the evaluator still calls the model failed (validation is failed): a disagreement between the evaluator and the solver, counted in the integrity document, with no machine taken for a liar. Empty without an answer.

digest.description: The digest of the settled row (smt-result/1): the same for the problem on every honest machine.

resource_count.description: The solver's resource counter after its last answered check.

fuel.description: The fuel of the session, counted from the solver's first instruction.
